operations.title: The analytic domain derived from the intrinsic Euler product is zero-free
operations.statement: The analytic character [a] maps to a^(-s) is absolutely summable for Re(s)>1. Absolute convergence of the logarithmic Euler product proves zeta(s) is nonzero throughout that domain. The current Carrier-side construction therefore reaches a zero-free region only; continuation, completion, functional-equation duality, and a global spectral operator remain underived.
operations.scope: Analytic-strength audit of the conditional formal Euler theorem; not a new classical zero-location theorem.

operations.title: Absolute-convergence zero-free gate
operations.procedure: For sigma=Re(s)>1, majorize sum_p p^(-sigma) by sum_(n>=2)n^(-sigma), expand logarithms of local factors, and verify absolute convergence to a finite value.
operations.expected_result: The Euler product converges to a nonzero value for Re(s)>1. A zero inside the absolutely convergent domain would falsify the claim.
